results.content: That represents a 10-percent decline in just three weeks. The newest poll shows Hispanic approval of Trump at 27 percent, compared with a 66 percent disapproval rating. This matters because Trump's political coalition has depended in part on making gains with Hispanic voters, particularly compared with Republicans' performance with the group in previous elections. A sustained decline in approval among Hispanic Americans would therefore represent a potentially important shift. Party: Democrats were most unfavorable toward Trump, with 98% disapproving, followed by independents at 62% disapproval. Meanwhile, Republicans were the most favorable toward Trump, with 82% approving of Trump's job performance.

Race: Black or African-American voters had the highest unfavorable opinion of Trump, with 88% disapproving, followed by Hispanic/Latino at 72% disapproval, Other at 68% disapproval and white at 59% disapproval.

USA TODAY’s Kinsey Crowley contributed to this report.
results.title: A new low for Trump approval rating triggered by ongoing war with Iran

results.content:
A bipartisan UnidosUS poll released in May found 67% of Latino voters nationally disapproved of Trump's job performance. Even in Florida, where Trump's standing among Hispanics was stronger than nationally, 51% disapproved and 44% approved.

The dissatisfaction does not necessarily mean Latino voters are returning to Democrats, however, an important distinction as both parties fight for an electorate that has become increasingly competitive.
